report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of daedalus/lanes/checks.py: unresolved_first_party_imports, imports_resolve, run_checks, with_markers, and BASELINE tuple. All docstring claims are kept; no broken assertions, inverted rules, or format-unpinned parsers found.

handoff.purpose: Define import resolution checks, baseline check tuple, run_checks orchestrator, and with_markers helper.

symbols.name: unresolved_first_party_imports
symbols.note: Static analysis of first-party imports; returns list of unresolved imports.

symbols.name: imports_resolve
symbols.note: Check wrapper that calls unresolved_first_party_imports and formats result.

symbols.name: BASELINE
symbols.note: Tuple of check functions in order: not_truncated, no_elision, parses, not_substituted, imports_resolve.

symbols.name: run_checks
symbols.note: Run baseline plus optional extra checks; returns first refusal reason or empty string.

symbols.name: with_markers
symbols.note: Returns a new CheckPolicy with updated elision markers.

claims.text: First-party imports in ``content`` that name nothing in the tree.
claims.why: Function returns list of strings describing imports that cannot be resolved to existing modules/names.

claims.text: The check is STATIC on purpose. Importing the file to find out whether its imports resolve would execute module-level code from an untrusted lane -- the one thing this repository refuses to do to decide whether to trust something.
claims.why: The function uses ast.parse and walks the AST; no imports are executed.

claims.text: Conservative by construction, because a false refusal costs real work: * only first-party roots are judged; * a missing MODULE is reported, since that cannot be a re-export; * a missing NAME is reported only when the module has no star-import and no module-level ``__getattr__``.
claims.why: Code checks first-party roots (line 327), reports missing modules (lines 331, 340), and skips if opaque (line 343).

claims.text: a parse failure is a different guard's business
claims.why: Line 319-321: parse exceptions return empty list.

claims.text: Checked for CREATED files too -- a brand-new test module against an invented API is exactly the failure this catches, and it has no original to compare against.
claims.why: imports_resolve calls unresolved_first_party_imports with attempt.proposed only; no comparison to original.

claims.text: Cheapest first. Order is load-bearing in one direction only -- the refusal a caller sees should be the most specific one available, and "does not parse" is more useful than "82% of definitions vanished" when both are true.
claims.why: BASELINE tuple order: not_truncated, no_elision, parses, not_substituted, imports_resolve. parses (syntax) comes before not_substituted (symbol survival).

claims.text: Run the baseline, then any lane-specific additions. "" means write it.
claims.why: Line 385: iterates over (*BASELINE, *extra). Returns empty string if no reason (line 394).

claims.text: FAIL-CLOSED, and this is the part worth not losing: a check that raises is reported as a refusal naming the crash.
claims.why: Lines 388-392: catches Exception and returns refusal string with exception info.

claims.text: A lane may pass ``extra`` to ADD checks. There is deliberately no argument for removing one from the baseline.
claims.why: Function signature has extra parameter; no parameter to remove checks.

claims.text: ``policy`` with this lane's own elision markers. Convenience only.
Grounding a model's PROSE against the tree -- audit_references, judge -- lives in daedalus/lanes/grounding.py.
claims.why: File daedalus/lanes/grounding.py not in this chunk; cannot verify.

observations.what: unresolved_first_party_imports returns empty list on parse failure, deferring to other guards.
imports_resolve only checks proposed content, not original (as designed for CREATED files).
run_checks catches all exceptions (noqa: BLE001) to fail closed.
